title: MCP server has no metadata-authoring tools: an AI client cannot create or update a flow through MCP (data-plane only)
body:
## Observation (objectstack 17.1.0, via hotcrm @ `ec4c5ac`, `objectstack dev -p 4001`)

`tools/list` on the built-in MCP server (`/api/v1/mcp`) returns 11 tools, all data-plane: `list_objects`, `describe_object`, `query_records`, `aggregate_records`, `get_record`, `create_record`, `update_record`, `delete_record`, `list_actions`, `run_action`, `validate_expression`. The server describes itself as operating on the app's **data objects**.

There is no tool that reads or writes **metadata**. In particular, an AI client connected through the advertised path (the dev banner's `claude mcp add --transport http … /api/v1/mcp`) cannot author a flow.

Meanwhile the flow designer's own save path is a plain metadata endpoint: `PUT /api/v1/meta/flow/<name>?mode=draft&package=<writable-pkg>` persists a draft (visible in Studio as an unpublished change, `_diagnostics.valid=true`), and package-level `POST /api/v1/packages/<pkg>/publish-drafts` (Studio's Publish) makes it live immediately, no restart. Verified end-to-end: an AI writing that endpoint produces a flow a human can open, edit, and publish in the designer, and the published flow really fires (a pending approval request is created on a matching record change). So the platform capability exists — it is just not reachable over MCP; an AI has to fall back to raw REST with session auth.

## Why it matters

The BYO-AI story routes external AI clients through MCP. For metadata work — "the AI writes the same artifact a human draws in the designer" — MCP currently offers nothing, so AI clients need bespoke REST plumbing and auth instead of the standard MCP connection.

## Minimal capability ask

Expose metadata authoring over MCP while keeping the existing safety shape:

- a draft-write tool (e.g. `upsert_flow_draft` or a scoped `put_metadata`) targeting a writable package, `mode=draft` only;
- either a publish tool mapping to package-level `publish-drafts`, or an explicit, documented boundary that publishing stays with humans in Studio (also a reasonable design — then say so);
- the same permission checks as the equivalent REST calls.

Flows alone would unlock the story; not asking for an arbitrary metadata surface in v1.

## Context

Found while producing promo video steedos-labs/video-studio#67 (internal). **Not blocking** that production — the REST metadata path suffices for filming — so no priority claim; filed as a capability finding.
